headline: 9 in 10 families borrow money for measles treatment in Bangladesh
summary: A new assessment reveals the devastating financial toll of the measles outbreak on poor households, with many exhausting savings to cover costs.
details: A study by the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS) and the IFRC found that 88.9% of affected households had to borrow money to meet treatment-related expenses.
At least 60.8% of families depleted their savings, while some were forced to sell assets or rely on donations to cope with the financial strain.
Although treatment at government hospitals is free, families face high costs for medicines, diagnostic tests, transport, and food, typically ranging between Tk 20,000 and Tk 40,000.
The burden is even heavier for low-income families who lose wages while caring for sick children, with some expenses reaching up to Tk 65,000.
As of July 31, at least 1.44 lakh patients, mostly children, have been hospitalized with measles or measles-like symptoms, with 810 deaths reported.
The assessment surveyed 2,746 households across 12 government medical college and district hospitals between May and June to identify vulnerable families for cash assistance.
caption:
Nearly 90% of families affected by the measles outbreak in Bangladesh are forced into debt to afford treatment.

A study by the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS) and the IFRC found that 88.9% of affected households had to borrow money to meet treatment-related expenses.

At least 60.8% of families depleted their savings, while some were forced to sell assets or rely on donations to cope with the financial strain.

Although treatment at government hospitals is free, families face high costs for medicines, diagnostic tests, transport, and food, typically ranging between Tk 20,000 and Tk 40,000.

The burden is even heavier for low-income families who lose wages while caring for sick children, with some expenses reaching up to Tk 65,000.

As of July 31, at least 1.44 lakh patients, mostly children, have been hospitalized with measles or measles-like symptoms, with 810 deaths reported.

The assessment surveyed 2,746 households across 12 government medical college and district hospitals between May and June to identify vulnerable families for cash assistance.

headline_marked: Gazipur's gas crisis: [[Severe shortage disrupts factories and lives]]
headline: Gazipur's gas crisis: Severe shortage disrupts factories and lives
summary: Industrial production slows as thousands of garment workers struggle to cook meals, some relying on firewood or skipping meals entirely.
details: A severe gas crisis in Gazipur's industrial belt is disrupting factory production and leaving thousands of garment workers struggling to cook meals at home.
Many factories are operating below capacity due to inadequate gas supply, reducing production and overall worker incomes.
Residents of workers' colonies, such as the Kuniya Workers' Colony in Board Bazar, are forced to use firewood for cooking, while others wait for unreliable gas supply.
Many workers go to bed without eating or leave for work without breakfast, relying on flattened rice, bread, and bananas due to the lack of gas.
According to Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited, Gazipur requires 550 MMCFD of gas per day, but only 300 MMCFD is being supplied.
The Gazipur Deputy Commissioner and district administration have discussed the issue with the relevant ministry to restore normal industrial production.
Authorities from several factories have reported severe production disruptions due to low gas pressure and irregular supply.
caption:
Gazipur's industrial belt is facing a severe gas crisis, with supply meeting only about 54% of the district's daily requirement.
